For centuries, Dunhuang was one of the great meeting points of the Silk Road. Different peoples, cultures and ideas came together here, giving rise to {{2}} forms of artistic and cultural expression. Today, digital technologies and artificial intelligence are once again transforming the way culture is preserved, created and shared.
paragraphs.cn: （中新社）——由中国国家版权局与世界知识产权组织（WIPO）共同主办的2026国际版权论坛于周一至周三在中国西北部甘肃省敦煌市举行。论坛以“数字与人工智能时代的版权与创意产业——保护文化遗产，赋能创新与创造力”为主题，汇聚各方参与者，讨论人工智能为版权带来的机遇与挑战、文化遗产的保护与活化，以及创意经济的发展。数百年来，敦煌一直是丝绸之路上重要的交汇点之一。不同民族、文化和思想在此汇聚，催生了非凡的艺术与文化表达形式。如今，数字技术和人工智能再次改变着文化被保存、创造和分享的方式。

paragraphs.en: What can Dunhuang’s millennia-old {{3}} teach us about creativity in the digital and AI age? And how can intellectual property continue to support cultural exchange and human creativity? Daren Tang, director general of WIPO, recently sat down with China News Service’s "East Meets West" for an {{4}} interview in Dunhuang to discuss cultural heritage, technological change and the future of human creativity. CNS: For centuries, different cultures met, {{5}} and came together in Dunhuang, giving rise to unique forms of artistic expression. In the digital and AI age, what can Dunhuang’s legacy of cultural exchange and creativity teach us about copyright and the development of the creative industries?
paragraphs.cn: 敦煌千年遗产能为数字与AI时代的创造力提供什么启示？知识产权如何继续支持文化交流与人类创造力？世界知识产权组织总干事邓鸿森近日在敦煌接受中新社“东西问”独家专访，探讨文化遗产、技术变革与人类创造力的未来。中新社：数百年来，不同文化在敦煌相遇、互动、交融，催生了独特的艺术表达形式。在数字与AI时代，敦煌文化交流与创造力的遗产能为版权和创意产业发展提供什么启示？

paragraphs.en: Daren Tang: Dunhuang is a fitting place to discuss copyright, creativity and culture. For centuries, this city was one of the great meeting points of the Silk Road. People came here from China, Central Asia, Persia, Europe and beyond, bringing not just goods, but also their stories, knowledge, beliefs and ways of seeing the world. Trade created those connections, but the {{6}} went far beyond {{7}}. Through connection, exchange and {{8}} between peoples, new ideas were {{9}}, different perspectives were combined and a unique culture was born.
paragraphs.cn: 邓鸿森：敦煌是讨论版权、创造力与文化的合适之地。数百年来，这座城市是丝绸之路上重要的交汇点之一。来自中国、中亚、波斯、欧洲及更远地方的人们来到这里，带来的不仅是货物，还有他们的故事、知识、信仰和看待世界的方式。贸易创造了这些联系，但其影响远远超出商业范畴。通过人与人之间的连接、交流与互动，新思想得以锻造，不同视角得以融合，一种独特的文化由此诞生。

paragraphs.en: There is an important lesson in this for us today. Cultures need exchange and engagement to remain alive and {{10}}. Copyright can help each culture preserve its {{11}} while giving it the confidence to exchange with other cultures. This is even more important in the age of digital technology and artificial intelligence. Creators need to know that their works can be protected, that they can {{12}} their creations, receive a fair return and continue to make a living from their creativity.
paragraphs.cn: 这对我们今天有重要启示。文化需要交流与互动才能保持活力和生机。版权可以帮助每种文化在保持自身认同的同时，赋予其与其他文化交流的自信。在数字技术和人工智能时代，这一点更为重要。创作者需要知道他们的作品能够得到保护，他们可以授权自己的创作、获得公平回报，并继续靠创造力谋生。

How do you see the challenges AI presents for copyright, and China’s role in the global creative economy? And the questions it raises for copyright are very real. If an AI company uses the works of writers, artists and other creators to train its models, should those creators be {{18}}? paragraphs.cn: 它不仅仅是又一项技术。就像电力或印刷机一样，它有潜力从根本上改变我们生活、工作和创作的方式。而它对版权提出的问题是真实存在的。如果一家AI公司使用作家、艺术家和其他创作者的作品来训练模型，这些创作者是否应该获得补偿？如果AI被用于生成音乐、图像或其他创意内容，谁应该拥有权利，谁应该在经济上受益？

(CNS) --The 2026 International Copyright Forum, jointly organized by the National Copyright Administration of China and the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO), was held in Dunhuang, northwest China's Gansu Province, from Monday to Wednesday.
Under the theme “Copyright and Creative Industries in the Digital and AI Age — Protecting Cultural Heritage, Empowering Innovation and Creativity”，the forum brought together participants to discuss the opportunities and challenges that artificial intelligence presents for copyright, the protection and revitalization of cultural heritage, and the development of the creative economy.
For centuries, Dunhuang was one of the great meeting points of the Silk Road. Different peoples, cultures and ideas came together here, giving rise to extraordinary forms of artistic and cultural expression. Today, digital technologies and artificial intelligence are once again transforming the way culture is preserved, created and shared.
What can Dunhuang’s millennia-old legacy teach us about creativity in the digital and AI age? And how can intellectual property continue to support cultural exchange and human creativity?
Daren Tang, director general of WIPO, recently sat down with China News Service’s "East Meets West" for an exclusive interview in Dunhuang to discuss cultural heritage, technological change and the future of human creativity.
CNS: For centuries, different cultures met, interacted and came together in Dunhuang, giving rise to unique forms of artistic expression. In the digital and AI age, what can Dunhuang’s legacy of cultural exchange and creativity teach us about copyright and the development of the creative industries?
Daren Tang: Dunhuang is a fitting place to discuss copyright, creativity and culture.
For centuries, this city was one of the great meeting points of the Silk Road. People came here from China, Central Asia, Persia, Europe and beyond, bringing not just goods, but also their stories, knowledge, beliefs and ways of seeing the world.
Trade created those connections, but the consequences went far beyond commerce. Through connection, exchange and engagement between peoples, new ideas were forged, different perspectives were combined and a unique culture was born.
There is an important lesson in this for us today. Cultures need exchange and engagement to remain alive and vibrant. Copyright can help each culture preserve its identity while giving it the confidence to exchange with other cultures.
This is even more important in the age of digital technology and artificial intelligence. Creators need to know that their works can be protected, that they can license their creations, receive a fair return and continue to make a living from their creativity.
By supporting creators, intellectual property also helps culture to endure, evolve and remain vibrant.
CNS: In recent years, the Dunhuang Academy has used digital technologies to bring this ancient cultural heritage to audiences around the world. As traditional culture moves into the digital space and becomes part of the material used to train AI, how can we balance wider access and creative use with respect for rights and interests?
Daren Tang: Digital Dunhuang is an excellent example of how technology can help bring culture and heritage to the world.
Not everyone can come to Dunhuang and see the caves and murals for themselves. But digital technology gives many more people, wherever they may be, the opportunity to experience and learn about Dunhuang. This is a very good example of technology serving culture and heritage.
In China, we are also seeing examples of traditional culture reaching international audiences through new media. A game such as Black Myth: Wukong introduces audiences around the world to Chinese literature, history, culture and historical sites through video games.
Digital technology at its best can be a bridge: a new way of connecting people and bringing Chinese culture and stories to global audiences.
Technology should empower culture, heritage and human creators, keeping them at the center of the intellectual property system.
CNS: Dunhuang’s art itself grew out of cultural exchange, interaction and constant reinvention. Today, AI is transforming the way content is created, while China’s online literature, games, film, television and animation are reaching more international audiences. How do you see the challenges AI presents for copyright, and China’s role in the global creative economy?
Daren Tang: Artificial intelligence is changing the way we create, distribute and consume content.
It is more than just another technology. Like electricity or the printing press, it has the potential to fundamentally change the way we live, work and create.
And the questions it raises for copyright are very real. If an AI company uses the works of writers, artists and other creators to train its models, should those creators be compensated? If AI is used to generate music, images or other creative content, who should own the rights, and who should benefit economically?
These are difficult questions, and we need to find the right balance between supporting technological innovation and protecting the interests of creators.
We should not look at AI only as a challenge, but also as an opportunity to empower and support a new generation of creators. There is one fundamental principle that should remain clear: human creators must remain at the heart of the copyright and intellectual property system.
Technology should not replace people or push them to the margins. It should empower, assist and support human creativity. We also need to make sure that AI does not create a single monoculture.
The aim is for diverse civilizations and cultures to continue flourishing in the age of AI. Training AI on material from across the world can help it draw on that diversity when creating new forms of art, rather than on a single cultural source.
China offers an interesting example of how the creative economy, cultural heritage and the digital economy can come together.
We just saw a presentation explaining how digital platforms are creating new films, music and stories to promote Chinese culture in other parts of the world.
This is also part of a much broader global trend. In Poland, for example, The Witcher draws on stories from medieval Poland. In Saudi Arabia, an animation studio has also created a game to promote Saudi culture to the rest of the world.
What we are seeing is a new convergence of the creative economy, cultural heritage and digital technology. This is creating new experiences for audiences, but it is also creating jobs, livelihoods and economic opportunities. I believe this will be an important part of the next chapter of the global creative economy.
CNS: The ancient Silk Road crossed mountains and deserts and helped connect civilizations across East and West. Today, digital networks allow culture and creativity to travel around the world almost instantaneously. If we think of these networks as a new “Digital Silk Road,” what should the intellectual property system seek above all to protect?
Daren Tang: Creativity and expression are a fundamental part of humanity. From ancient cave art to stone tools and instruments made from bones, human beings have been creating for tens of thousands of years, and perhaps much longer.
The role of copyright is to support that human spirit of creativity and expression. Even in the age of AI and digital technologies, the copyright system must continue to support it. Otherwise, we risk losing something very precious and fundamental to humanity.
Technologies come and go. Even AI, a technology that may come along only once every few hundred years, is still a technology. The human spirit has been with us for hundreds of thousands of years. It is something more fundamental and enduring.
The role of the intellectual property system is therefore not to push away these technologies, but to make sure they serve the human spirit of creativity, expression and connection.
Biography
Daren Tang，World Intellectual Property Organization Director General. He is a national of Singapore, began his first six-year mandate as Director General of the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) on October 1, 2020 and was reappointed on April 21, 2026 for a second term that will run from October 1, 2026 through September 30, 2032.
His last appointment before joining WIPO was Chief Executive of the Intellectual Property Office of Singapore (IPOS) where he transformed IPOS from a traditional IP registry into an innovation agency, enhancing Singapore's IP ecosystem and strengthening international collaborations.

通过支持创作者，知识产权也帮助文化得以延续、演变并保持活力。中新社：近年来，敦煌研究院利用数字技术将这一古老文化遗产带给世界各地的观众。随着传统文化进入数字空间并成为训练AI的素材，我们如何在大范围获取和创造性使用与尊重权益之间取得平衡？邓鸿森：“数字敦煌”是技术如何帮助将文化与遗产带给世界的绝佳范例。并非每个人都能亲自来到敦煌，亲眼看到洞窟和壁画。

但数字技术让更多身处各地的人有机会体验和了解敦煌。这是技术服务文化与遗产的很好例子。在中国，我们也看到传统文化通过新媒体触达国际受众的例子。像《黑神话：悟空》这样的游戏通过电子游戏向世界各地观众介绍中国文学、历史、文化和历史遗迹。数字技术最好的状态可以成为一座桥梁：一种连接人们、将中国文化和故事带给全球受众的新方式。

技术应当赋能文化、遗产和人类创作者，使他们始终处于知识产权体系的中心。中新社：敦煌艺术本身就是在文化交流、互动和不断再造中生长出来的。如今，AI正在改变内容创作方式，而中国的网络文学、游戏、影视和动画正触达更多国际受众。您如何看待AI对版权带来的挑战，以及中国在全球创意经济中的角色？邓鸿森：人工智能正在改变我们创作、传播和消费内容的方式。

它不仅仅是又一项技术。就像电力或印刷机一样，它有潜力从根本上改变我们生活、工作和创作的方式。而它对版权提出的问题是真实存在的。如果一家AI公司使用作家、艺术家和其他创作者的作品来训练模型，这些创作者是否应该获得补偿？如果AI被用于生成音乐、图像或其他创意内容，谁应该拥有权利，谁应该在经济上受益？

这些是难题，我们需要在支持技术创新与保护创作者利益之间找到恰当的平衡。我们不应只把AI视为挑战，也应将其视为赋能和支持新一代创作者的机会。有一个基本原则应当保持明确：人类创作者必须始终处于版权和知识产权体系的核心。技术不应取代人，也不应把人推向边缘。它应当赋能、协助和支持人类创造力。

我们还需要确保AI不会造成单一文化。目标是让多元文明和文化在AI时代继续繁荣。用来自世界各地的素材训练AI，可以帮助它在创造新艺术形式时汲取这种多样性，而不是依赖单一文化来源。中国提供了一个有趣的例子，展示创意经济、文化遗产和数字经济如何融合。我们刚刚看到一场演示，介绍数字平台如何创造新的电影、音乐和故事，以在世界其他地区推广中国文化。

这也是更广泛全球趋势的一部分。例如在波兰，《巫师》借鉴了中世纪波兰的故事。在沙特阿拉伯，一家动画工作室也制作了一款游戏，向世界其他地区推广沙特文化。我们看到的是创意经济、文化遗产和数字技术的新融合。这不仅为观众创造新体验，也在创造就业、生计和经济机会。

我相信这将成为全球创意经济下一篇章的重要组成部分。中新社：古丝绸之路穿越山脉和沙漠，帮助连接东西方文明。如今，数字网络让文化和创造力几乎瞬间传遍世界。如果我们把这些网络视为一条新的“数字丝绸之路”，知识产权体系首先应当保护什么？邓鸿森：创造力和表达是人类的基本组成部分。

从古代洞穴艺术到石器和骨制乐器，人类已经创作了数万年，或许更久。版权的作用是支持人类这种创造与表达的精神。即使在AI和数字技术时代，版权体系也必须继续支持它。否则，我们就有可能失去对人类而言非常珍贵和根本的东西。技术来了又去。

即便是AI——一种可能数百年才出现一次的技术——仍然只是一种技术。人类精神已经伴随我们数十万年。它是更根本、更持久的东西。因此，知识产权体系的作用不是排斥这些技术，而是确保它们服务于人类的创造力、表达和连接精神。简介

他是新加坡国民，于2020年10月1日开始担任世界知识产权组织（WIPO）总干事首个六年任期，并于2026年4月21日获连任，第二个任期将从2026年10月1日持续至2032年9月30日。加入WIPO之前，他最近的职务是新加坡知识产权局（IPOS）局长，其间他将IPOS从传统知识产权注册机构转型为创新机构，增强了新加坡知识产权生态系统并加强了国际合作。

articles.fullText:
American voters have handed Democrats control of both houses of Congress in the midterms, decisively rejecting Republicans in historically red states and shifting the balance of power in Washington, DC.
Here are five key takeaways.
Democratic victories exceed polls
The polls in the run up to election day pointed to a likely Democrat majority in the Senate and almost certain control of the House, but the party ended up outperforming even those positive indicators, flipping multiple Republican strongholds.
Leading 54-44 in the Senate, flipping seven seats from the Republicans with two still to be called, was beyond the dreams of most Democrats. In the House, the party already has a majority, with over 60 seats still to be called, and Hakeem Jeffries is set to become the country’s first Black speaker.
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries greets volunteers during a midterm election night watch party in Washington, DC, November 3, 2026. 
The Republican defeat will have major consequences for both the Trump administration and the country at large over the next two years as well as the 2028 election cycle.
Trump says he accepts results
US President Donald Trump said he would respect the midterm results in interviews with the New York Times and Fox News. He acknowledged that the price of gas may have contributed to the Republican defeat but insisted he was right to go to war with Iran.
The president, who has historically low approval ratings, said that if he had been on the ballot, the result would have been different. However, the gains the Republicans had made with Hispanic and rural voters under Trump were wiped out in many areas, amid concerns over an immigration crackdown and the cost of living, and gas in particular.
Trump also said he had no regrets about endorsing candidates who struggled on the campaign trail, including Darline Graham in South Carolina and Ken Paxton in Texas, both of whom lost in traditionally red states.
Democrats strike in deep red territory
Democratic candidates have been victorious in what were until recently seen as unassailably Republican territory, from Kansas and Texas to South Carolina in the Senate.
Midterm results are displayed during an election night event with James Talarico, a Democrat from Texas, Austin, Texas, US, November 3, 2026. 
That Texas elected a Democratic senator in James Talarico and – even more strikingly – Gina Hinojosa as governor is a seismic change in the southern state, where Hispanic voters appear to have deserted the Republicans. Similarly, victories in Kansas, South Carolina and potentially Alaska marked major changes. Whether they are held in six years' time or not, they are likely to give Democrats a major advantage in the next cycle.
The party's candidates also secured two momentous firsts: Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan will become the US's first Muslim senator, and Keisha Lance Bottoms, who won the Georgia governor race, is set to be the nation's first elected Black woman governor. However, while the results were spectacular for the Democrats and individual candidates shone, the party brand remains broadly unpopular.
Balance of power flips
From a trifecta to divided government, after endorsing the Republican agenda in 2024, Americans decisively rejected the party in 2026. The results have major implications for the final two years of the president's time in office.
With comfortable majorities in both houses of Congress, the Democrats will not only be a major check on the administration's domestic agenda and appointments but will also have the space to accept some dissent within its broad coalition.
The Democratic grip on the domestic agenda could lead Trump to make more use of executive orders and focus more on foreign policy, where Congress has less power to intervene.
The 2028 presidential race begins
The permanent campaign is a feature of the US political system, and attention is already turning to the 2028 election cycle.
The comprehensive reelection of Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff in Georgia and Roy Cooper flipping North Carolina, also in the Senate, will do nothing to harm the buzz behind them, while Josh Shapiro was comfortably reelected as Pennsylvania's governor.
The midterms also unearthed a series of new potential stars, from Talarico and El-Sayed to Adam Hamilton in Kansas, Annie Andrews in South Carolina and Josh Turek in Iowa.
There were no breakout performances for the Republicans, though Byron Donalds narrowly held off his opponent to become Florida's first Black governor. For 2028 frontrunners like JD Vance and Marco Rubio, who are closely associated with the administration, the results will make nervous reading.

articles.fullText:
Located in east China's Fujian Province, the coastal city of Xiamen is emerging as an important hub for marine science, ocean conservation and international cooperation on ocean governance.
The 2026 World Ocean Week, which kicked off in the city under the theme "Safeguard the deep blue together, foster human-ocean harmony" has brought together government officials, experts and representatives of international organizations to explore ways to advance global ocean governance and marine sustainability.
With marine ecological conservation at its core, the event highlights the importance of scientific research, policy coordination, local practices and public engagement in translating global commitments into concrete action.
A report released during the 2026 World Ocean Week highlights China's contributions to global ocean governance and the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity. Compiled by the China Institute for Marine Affairs under the Ministry of Natural Resources, the report details China's contributions to the Agreement under the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea on the Conservation and Sustainable Use of Marine Biological Diversity of Areas beyond National Jurisdiction, known as the BBNJ Agreement.
It outlines China's efforts to share marine expertise, bridge differences between developed and developing countries, and advance international cooperation.
According to the report, China has signed marine cooperation agreements with more than 50 countries and international organizations and jointly established over 40 marine research centers and laboratories.
International experts attending the event highlighted China's growing influence in the global ocean economy and its contributions to international marine conservation. They also pointed to Xiamen's strengths in marine research and its potential role in supporting global ocean governance.
Vaipo Mataora, permanent secretary of the Ministry of Infrastructure of the Cook Islands, noted in his remarks at the opening ceremony of World Ocean Week that international cooperation is essential to addressing the challenges facing small island states in ocean governance.
"Small island states hold vast ocean spaces, but we have small populations and limited technical capacity. We need shared science, shared data and shared skills," he said, emphasizing the importance of sharing scientific knowledge, data and expertise to support marine conservation and sustainable development.
Alfredo Giron, director of the Ocean Agenda at the World Economic Forum's Centre for Nature and Climate, said in an interview with China News Network that China's influence on the global ocean economy is undeniable, given its significant role in sectors such as offshore wind energy and fisheries.
"It's undeniable that China is one of the major influences in the global ocean economy," he said, noting that China's development of marine-related industries has a considerable impact globally.
José María Figueres, former president of Costa Rica, said in an interview with China News Network that Xiamen has a strong foundation for contributing to global ocean governance, citing its ecosystem of universities, research centers and marine laboratories.
"Xiamen has an ecosystem of universities, research centers, ocean laboratories that no other place has," he said, adding that the city could make a significant contribution to the implementation of the BBNJ Agreement.
Figueres also spoke highly of China's efforts in advancing global ocean governance, particularly its cooperation with developing countries. He noted that China has worked with countries with fewer resources to conduct joint research and share knowledge.
"There is no other country in the world today that is doing the things that China is doing in working together with other countries to help understand better of the ocean and the potential that it has in our livelihoods," he said, highlighting China's role in helping bridge scientific gaps within the global community.
As the international community moves from negotiating agreements to implementing them, stronger scientific support, knowledge sharing and cooperation among countries will be essential to addressing the challenges facing the ocean.
Xiamen's experience in bringing together marine research, ecological conservation and economic development offers a local perspective on how coastal cities can contribute to these shared global goals.

November 3 is UNESCO's International Day for Biosphere Reserves. Designated under UNESCO's Man and the Biosphere (MAB) Programme, these areas bring together biodiversity conservation, scientific research and sustainable development.
They demonstrate how protecting ecosystems can go hand in hand with supporting local communities.
Jiuzhaigou Valley, a UNESCO MAB Reserve in Sichuan Province, southwest China. 
The urgency of biodiversity action was underscored at the 17th meeting of the Conference of the Parties (COP17) to the Convention on Biological Diversity, which concluded in Yerevan, Armenia, on October 31, 2026.
The meeting completed the first global review of collective progress under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework.
The framework sets 23 targets for 2030, including conserving at least 30 percent of terrestrial and inland water areas, as well as coastal and marine areas. The review found that the world remains off track to meet these targets.
Parties adopted nearly 50 decisions and the Yerevan Pathway, which identifies priorities for accelerating implementation, strengthening monitoring and reporting, and increasing support for developing countries.
A view of the Nanji Islands Biosphere Reserve in Zhejiang Province, east China. 
A longer-term roadmap was adopted at the 5th World Congress of Biosphere Reserves in Hangzhou, China, in 2025.
The Hangzhou Declaration and the Hangzhou Strategic Action Plan for UNESCO's MAB Programme and its World Network of Biosphere Reserves (2026-2035) provide a framework for the network's work over the next decade.
The plan sets three strategic objectives: advancing environmental agreements, strengthening the MAB network, and advancing research and knowledge-sharing.
It also includes 34 voluntary action targets and encourages cooperation with Indigenous Peoples and local communities.
A Sichuan snub-nosed monkey is seen at the Shennongjia Biosphere Reserve in Hubei Province, central China. 
China is home to 36 UNESCO biosphere reserves, including the Daqingshan Biosphere Reserve in Inner Mongolia and the Zhouzhi Biosphere Reserve in Shaanxi, both designated in 2025.
Beyond these designated reserves, wider restoration efforts in China offer further examples of how ecological recovery can benefit people and nature.
In Baotou, Inner Mongolia, wetlands along the Yellow River provide habitat for around 100,000 migratory birds each year. The area supports 242 bird species, 165 more than in the late 1990s.
At Dianchi Lake in Yunnan Province, restoration efforts have helped revive underwater ecosystems, with the density of submerged plants increasing from less than 2% to 60%.
Flocks of seagulls gather near Haigeng Dam on Dianchi Lake in Kunming, Yunnan Province, southwest China. 
Technology is also supporting conservation. At Dianchi Lake, an AI-powered monitoring system uses high-definition cameras, drones and deep-learning algorithms to identify bird species, count populations and record their behavior.
It has achieved an accuracy rate of more than 90%, providing data to support research into bird migration, breeding habits and wetland health.
China is also contributing to global biodiversity efforts. It has contributed 400 million yuan (about $60 million) to the Kunming Biodiversity Fund. The fund has approved 31 projects across 45 developing countries.
During COP17, nine projects worth about $4.5 million were approved under the first phase of its third funding round.
A view of Fontainebleau Forest, part of the Fontainebleau and Gâtinais Biosphere Reserve in France. 
UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves now comprises 797 sites across 145 countries, covering 7.5 million square kilometers, or more than 5% of the Earth's terrestrial surface.
As countries work to turn biodiversity commitments into action, biosphere reserves offer practical ways to connect ecosystem conservation, scientific knowledge and sustainable development.

汪文斌表示，中国和柬埔寨是命运与共、相互支持的真朋友。中国将继续支持柬埔寨探索符合本国国情的发展道路，并愿深化治党治国经验交流，进一步推进双边关系。索西潘表示，保持清晰的战略方向并将长远愿景转化为人民生活的实际改善，是所有国家面临的共同挑战。他说，在地缘政治紧张局势升级的背景下，中国通过战略规划应对挑战的经验为其他国家提供了宝贵借鉴。他还表示，柬中两国应进一步巩固长期友谊，为两国和地区的和平、稳定与繁荣作出贡献。宋杜积极评价中国对全球治理的贡献，称中国近几十年的发展经验不仅对中国人民具有重要意义，也对世界经济和全球发展产生深远影响。

活动上还放映了中央广播电视总台一批精品节目的宣传片，让与会者身临其境地感受中国新质生产力的蓬勃活力。
